_comment:
Seeing stars. A damped wander: six whole-actor lurches whose amplitude decays (0.055 -> 0.045 -> 0.034 -> 0.024 -> 0.014 -> 0.008 -> 0), each one eased so the body DRIFTS, with the head snapping the opposite way on every swing because `parts` do not tween and a lolling head should pop. The halo is faked - there is no orbit channel - by spawning sparkles at the role's overhead mark at alternating heights (0.50 / 0.44 / 0.52 / 0.47) while the body wanders underneath them; the eye reads the changing gap as circling. Tier 1-3 only: whole-actor moves, ad-hoc `parts` on `head`, two expressions, stock effects and stock sounds. No clip, no new art, so it casts on every rig ToonRigRepair has touched.

What it deliberately does NOT animate: feet. Nobody in limited animation staggers with their legs; the footsteps sound does that job for free, and a legless drift is what the whole form is built on.

beats._comment: the moment it lands, before any drift - the anticipation is this held beat of registering it
the halo sits above the head at the mark; anchoring resolves at shot start, so it stays put while the body wanders under it - which is exactly the read we want
swing 1, the widest. dx is an offset from the bound mark, so alternating signs with shrinking magnitude is a damped wander that ends home.
one last star after the body has nearly settled - the head clears slower than the feet
back on the mark. Position carries to the end of the SCENE, so a wander that does not come home is permanent.
empty transform set = head upright again, at the rig's own rest pose
